correctness.rationale: The evaluation/signature correspondence is exact. A rank-d map identifies the trace set with cosets of its kernel meeting the weight-three layer. All k-subspaces appear once in a uniquely parameterized RREF enumeration. C++ normalized-coset enumeration and independent Python whole-coset enumeration agree on all seven test profiles, including all 788035 kernels at n=9 and their entire coverage distribution; Gaussian binomial totals certify state exhaustiveness. Explicit signatures cover all required patterns at n=6,7,8,10, and one n=9 witness has exactly 63 patterns. An orbit BFS using adjacent transpositions of S_9 partitions all 2304 maximizers into four orbits of sizes 1260,756,252,36. The finite enumeration is not claimed beyond these parameters.

value.rationale: Sparse fixed-weight parity constraints are natural in finite concept learning and short-XOR/coding theory. The sharp first six-query threshold gives a precise nontrivial one-pattern shortage (63 of 64) immediately below attainability; the exhaustive classification of all 2304 near-covers into four symmetry types identifies a natural extremal boundary, rather than an arbitrary specimen or minor numerical gain. The result is a self-contained finite invariant with explicit verification and motivates higher-dimensional restricted sumset study; no downstream theorem is asserted.
